adopted.rationale: Least friction with an explicit safety gate; a single validation surface that also fills the PR description; and desktop one-click distribution reusing the tiny self-contained bundle.
adopted.summary: A commit-time consent gate in submit_document backed by a per-user store (set_consent/manage_consent plus a consent CLI); a renderPrDescription in the validator returned by submit_document AND rendered onto the PR body by the App webhook; an optional diagrams schema field rendered as native fences and in the viewer under strict mermaid; removal of the Action so the App webhook is the only validation path; and an .mcpb manifest + mcpb:pack script wrapping the self-contained dist.

requirements.text: Global install must not silently act on a repo; ask per-repo with Always/Once/Never and a reset path.
submit_document returns a ready-to-use PR description, and the App sets it on the PR from the committed doc.
Optional Mermaid diagrams render in the PR body and the viewer.
One validation path (the App webhook); remove the Action.
One-click desktop install via .mcpb, hosted in the same repo.

trials.outcome: Would still act everywhere by default.
trials.what: Have the viewer show a friendly 'install the app' prompt on a 404 for repos without the App.
trials.why_abandoned: User wanted explicit per-repo opt-in, not silent-attempt-then-nudge.

trials.outcome: Avoids wasted work on a decline.
trials.what: Prompt for consent at the start of the flow (before the interview).
Store the consent decision as a file committed in the repo.
trials.why_abandoned: User chose a per-user central store at ~/.review-assist/consent.json.

trials.outcome: Would duplicate the structured fields and go stale.
trials.what: Store the rendered PR description as a field inside the Intent Document JSON.
trials.why_abandoned: The description is rendered from the doc on demand (renderPrDescription); the doc stays the single source of truth.

trials.what: Bundle node_modules into the .mcpb per the CLI default.
trials.why_abandoned: The esbuild output is self-contained; the bundle is ~155KB with just dist + manifest.

assumptions.assumption: Commit time (submit_document) is the right point to ask for consent, per the user's explicit choice, rather than at the start of the flow.
assumptions.how_to_verify: Watch first-run UX on real repos; measure wasted work on declines.
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: A 'Never' answer wastes the interview/distillation work that already ran; the gate would need to move earlier.

assumptions.assumption: The authoring agent already holds full change context, so local transcript hydration is unnecessary when dogfooding from a Cowork session.
assumptions.how_to_verify: Review the document against the actual diff and conversation.
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: The document could miss rationale that only lived in the session; meta.interview reflects the real (small) interview.

assumptions.assumption: GitHub renders our Mermaid fences natively and the viewer's securityLevel strict safely renders repo-authored diagrams.
assumptions.how_to_verify: Open a PR with a diagram and load the guided viewer.
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: Diagrams break or become an injection vector in the viewer.

assumptions.assumption: The App webhook (non-blocking check + comment + PR-body) fully replaces the Action, and the CLI covers teams that still want their own CI.
assumptions.how_to_verify: Confirm the webhook posts check+comment+body and the review-assist CLI still runs the same checks.
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: Teams relying on Action-based enforcement lose it with no path.

assumptions.assumption: The self-contained esbuild bundle needs no node_modules inside the .mcpb.
assumptions.how_to_verify: Install the .mcpb in the Claude desktop app and invoke a tool.
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: The bundle fails to start after install.

assumptions.assumption: Managing a marked block in the PR body (and only setting an empty body) never clobbers a human-written description.
assumptions.how_to_verify: Open a PR with an existing body and confirm only the marked block changes.
assumptions.impact_if_wrong: The App could overwrite a reviewer's prose in the PR body.

diagrams.caption: Global install, per-repo opt-in. Decisions persist in ~/.review-assist/consent.json; manage_consent resets them.
diagrams.mermaid:
flowchart TD
    A[submit_document] --> B{consent for this repo}
    B -->|enabled or once| C[validate, write Intent Document, return pr_description]
    B -->|disabled| D[no-op: skip and tell user how to re-enable]
    B -->|unknown| E[ask user: Always or Just this time or Never]
    E --> F[set_consent] --> A
diagrams.title: Consent decision at commit time

open_questions.context: User chose commit-time gating; revisit if wasted work on declines is annoying in practice.
open_questions.question: Should a 'Never' short-circuit earlier than commit time so the interview isn't wasted?

out_of_scope: A full Cowork/Claude Code plugin (MCP + skills + slash commands) and a marketplace

problem.statement: Review Assist installs globally but would silently act on every repository, produced no PR description, could not carry diagrams, and shipped a redundant GitHub Action alongside the App — friction and safety gaps blocking real adoption.
user_asks: We should ask user while committing if they want the review assist to work on it and if not.. should it be never or only this time. There should also be a way to remove from the no op list.
We should also generate a PR description right as part of the intent.
Also as part of it, it should allow generating mermaid diagrams and everything.
this github app webhook should be the only path as we now have a github app. No need for the github action right ?
Shouldn't it be part of intent doc itself ? ... If the description is not empty already, then add another section to the PR

tour.attention: The unknown/disabled branches in submit_document must run before any write.
tour.title: Per-repo consent gate at commit time
tour.what: New consent.ts stores per-user decisions in ~/.review-assist/consent.json; submit_document gates on it — returning consent_required (Always/Once/Never) for unknown repos and skipping disabled ones — and gains set_consent + manage_consent tools plus a consent CLI subcommand. The guide tells the agent to relay the prompt at submit time.
tour.why: Installed globally, Review Assist must not act on a repo without the user's say-so; the write is the point of no return.

tour.attention: diagramsMarkdown must not flatten multi-line mermaid; the webhook must not clobber a human-written body.
tour.title: PR description generated from the intent — in the tool and on the PR
tour.what: A new renderPrDescription in the validator (problem, approach, diagrams, assumptions) exported and returned by submit_document as pr_description; mermaid newlines are preserved rather than flattened. The GitHub App webhook then renders the same description onto the PR body from the committed doc — setting an empty body, else managing a delimited marker block so author prose is preserved.
tour.why: The PR opens self-describing with no copy-paste or gh step; the doc stays the single source of truth and the guided-review link still comes from the webhook.

tour.attention: Use plain-ASCII mermaid; strict security neutralizes repo-authored source.
tour.title: Mermaid diagrams as a first-class part of the format
tour.what: Optional top-level diagrams field in the schema (title/mermaid/caption) plus TS type; the example gains a sample sequence diagram; the viewer renders diagrams via mermaid.js (securityLevel strict) in a Diagrams section.
tour.why: Some changes are far clearer as a picture; GitHub renders fences natively and the viewer renders them too.

tour.attention: The CLI is intentionally retained; the big diff hunk here is the deleted generated dist/main.cjs.
tour.title: Retire the GitHub Action
tour.what: Delete apps/github-action and its workflow; drop it from the root workspaces/build; rewrite README and SPEC so the App is the single validation and experience surface. The review-assist CLI remains for self-hosted CI.
tour.why: The App webhook already runs the checks and posts the check+comment with zero config, making the Action redundant.

tour.attention: No node_modules needed thanks to the esbuild bundle.
tour.title: Package the MCP server as a one-click .mcpb
tour.what: Add manifest.json (stdio node to dist/index.js) and an mcpb:pack script; .mcpbignore keeps the bundle to manifest + dist + README; the ~155KB .mcpb ships as a release asset (gitignored). Landing gains a Download-.mcpb option and switches the Claude Code command to -s user.
tour.why: One-click desktop install with no terminal, reusing the self-contained bundle; global -s user makes the server available in every repo.
